# Vite

Build tool and dev server for the [[stickfps]] client — `vite ^8.1.1` with `@vitejs/plugin-react
^6.0.3`, producing the static bundle that is deployed separately from the game server under
[[split-frontend-backend-hosting]].

## The property that shapes the deployment

**`VITE_*` variables are inlined at build time, not read at runtime.** `VITE_SERVER_URL`,
`VITE_SERVER_PORT`, `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` are baked into the bundle by
`vite build`. Changing the backend address is therefore a **rebuild and redeploy**, not a
configuration change — which is why the deployment runbook is ordered backend-first: the server URL
must exist before the frontend can be built against it.

The corollary is a security one worth stating: anything with a `VITE_` prefix is public by
construction. It is visible in the shipped JavaScript. Only publishable values belong there — the
anon key in {{supabase}} is designed for that, a service key never would be.

## Vitest

`vitest ^4.1.10` on both sides of the repo, sharing Vite's transform pipeline, plus `jsdom ^29.1.1`
and `@testing-library/react ^16.3.2` on the client. 52 client tests, all over pure functions;
[[playwright]] covers anything needing a real GL context.

The server keeps a `vitest.config.ts` that exists for a **single line**: `fileParallelism: false`,
working around a vitest 4 worker-loading failure on Windows under CommonJS. Worth recording as the
kind of config file that looks arbitrary a year later — the reason is in `PROGRESS.md`, not beside
the setting, and that gap is exactly where [[documentation-drift]] starts.

## Toolchain shape

`tsc` and `oxlint ^1.71.0` both run clean, and `vite build` is clean. Two build pipelines and twelve
runtime dependencies across client and server put [[stickfps]] firmly on the other side of
[[zero-dependency-no-build-step]] from the coursework repositories — the same instinct reappears one
layer down as an absolute rule about assets rather than about tooling, in [[no-external-assets]].
